Impact and entrepreneurship
An entrepreneurial university
At Chalmers, entrepreneurial action is a mindset that permeates our research, education, how we create impact, and how we collaborate with society. We see entrepreneurship as the ability to identify opportunities, take initiative, and create value – whether that happens in a lab, a startup, a classroom, or in collaboration with industry.

Research
Interactive 3D technology reveals hidden tumours during surgery
Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology, and the University of Gothenburg, in col­lab­o­ra­tion with Sahlgrenska University Hospital, all in Sweden, have developed a new technology that creates an interactive 3D image of the liver during surgery. This could make it easier, for example, to remove a tumour hidden beneath the organ’s surface. The technology has now been used in surgery on a patient for the first time.

Press release
How thousands of self-driving electric taxis could be coordinated
Imagine ordering a ride on your phone and a self-driving electric car arrives within minutes. It picks you up, perhaps shares your ride with other passengers, and takes you to your destination – without a driver and without emissions. At the same time, thousands of similar vehicles move around the city, recharge their batteries when needed, and reposition themselves to be where the next passenger is likely to appear. Behind this seamless experience lies a complex puzzle. Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology have developed methods that could help thousands of vehicles plan their operations, charging and routes – even when the future is uncertain.

Research
Researchers in exile thrive when con­tribut­ing
Researchers in vulnerable conditions find it easier to establish themselves in new academic envi­ron­ments when they can contribute their own knowledge rather than simply receive support. A new study from Chalmers shows that reciprocal rela­tion­ships create strong networks, which in turn can lead to pub­li­ca­tions, research funding and new career oppor­tu­ni­ties.

News
Chalmers to help build Europe’s quantum software infra­struc­ture
As quantum computers become more powerful, making different quantum tech­nolo­gies work together, and alongside con­ven­tional super­com­put­ers, is becoming an increas­ingly important challenge. A new European initiative, EuroQSS (Universal European Quantum Software Stack), brings together 13 partners from industry and academia, Chalmers being one, to develop a common software framework designed to make this possible.
